TIMING AND RESOURCE PLAN (computed from the 7series delay model, 70% of the period per stage). Write the RTL to this plan: use each named template so synthesis infers the planned primitive; after synthesis a planned DSP or BRAM that comes out as LUTs or registers fails the gate.
- datapath hough_projection_and_bin_update (clock period 10.0 ns, stage budget 7.0 ns; one stage unpipelined would be 19.63 ns): 6 register stages, latency 6 clocks from the source register.
    x_times_cos (mul) -> dsp: DSP48E1 multiply fully pipelined: free-running registered operands, then `m <= a_r * b_r;`, then `p <= m (+ c);` (AREG/BREG, MREG, PREG; a following add of another product or a constant can go in the P stage; a MAC is `acc <= (first ? 0 : acc) + m`); no asynchronous reset on any of them, and no `use_dsp` attribute on the module (measured: it pulls other arithmetic into DSPs, 21 slices for 4 MACs; use it on the product signal only if inference fails) [5 x 8 multiply: the part has DSP48E1 slices free (1 slice); the narrower operand (5 bits) is close to the 4-bit 'too small' limit: check the widths against the spec (signed operands need their sign bit)]

    projection_sum (add) -> carry: adder or subtractor `s <= a + b;` on the carry chain (CARRY4); a sum of three or more terms is a tree of two-input adds, registered between levels if the plan says so [adder: carry chain]

    bin_address_select (logic) -> lut: plain LUT logic [plain logic: no hard resource fits]

    saturating_increment (add) -> carry: adder or subtractor `s <= a + b;` on the carry chain (CARRY4); a sum of three or more terms is a tree of two-input adds, registered between levels if the plan says so [adder: carry chain]

## How to read this

An estimate from the 7-series delay model (version 2026-11-12b), not a measurement. "Latency" is what the plan implies, counted from the source register. The operand widths are the architect's: it wrote the coordinate as 5 bits (spec.md says 0 to 31) and the cosine as 8 bits, but a cosine of +128 needs 9 bits signed, and the reference RTL uses 8-bit coordinates (9 x 9 signed). The DSP choice is the same either way; the planner now flags a multiply whose narrower operand is within 2 bits of its 'too small for a DSP' limit. The closure run used the plan from model version 2026-11-12a (TIMING_PLAN_model_a.md); this file is the same architecture planned with 2026-11-12b. Why 5 x 8 here and 9 x 9 in the delay model: the plan sizes each multiply at the operand widths the architect wrote in architecture.yaml (5 and 8 bits), while 9 x 9 is only the size the calibration build measured; the DSP stages do not depend on the width up to 25 x 18.
